sites.name: Jefferson DSP&P Railroad Depot & Station Site
overview: The Jefferson Denver, South Park & Pacific depot is a surviving circa-1880 combination passenger-and-freight depot and one of the few intact structures from the historic narrow-gauge network.

timeline.text: The depot served the Denver, South Park & Pacific system and remained in active railroad use until 1937.

sites.name: Abel Mineral Land Prospect
sites.location: Tarryall Springs Mining District, Park County
overview: The Abel Mineral Land Prospect, also documented as the Abel Property and Holmes Ranch or Abell Ranch, is a tungsten prospect in the Tarryall Springs mining district of Park County. Colorado Geological Survey documentation describes a 160-acre property south of U.S. 24 with scheelite-bearing skarn and several small workings.

timeline.text: Geologic work cited by the Colorado Geological Survey documented the Abel Property and Holmes Ranch deposits and their workings.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey research places the property in section 15, Township 12 South, Range 72 West, near the southwestern end of the Firefly belt. The deposits occur in steeply dipping, northeast-striking lenses containing quartz, garnet, epidote, and vesuvianite. Scheelite was reported in a roughly three-foot garnet-rich zone traced for about 1,300 feet. Documented workings included a 36-foot shaft and six small pits.

sourceReferences.title: Colorado Geological Survey RS-21 — Precambrian Tungsten and Copper-Zinc Skarn Deposits of South-Central Colorado

sites.name: Allegheny Placer
sites.location: Mosquito Pass area near the Park–Lake county line
overview: Allegheny Placer is a named high-elevation placer site near Mosquito Pass, recorded in Park County and preserved on U.S. Geological Survey mapping of the Leadville and Climax area.

Federal mineral-resource records classify it as a past producer associated with gold and uranium. The mapped point represents the documented placer landscape rather than one precisely surveyed surviving cut, shaft, or item of equipment.

timeline.text: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 235 published detailed Leadville-area mapping that labels the site as the Alleghany Placer.
A U.S. Bureau of Mines reporter entered the Allegheny Placer in the federal Mineral Resources Data System as a Park County past producer associated with gold and uranium.

moreHistory: The site lies close to the Park–Lake county line in the Mosquito Pass area. Federal mineral-resource records place the Allegheny Placer in Park County, while some modern map services may assign nearby features differently because of the boundary.

The identification point at approximately 39.27721, -106.18308 is a landscape-level anchor for the named placer. It does not establish the condition, exact extent, or accessibility of surviving workings.

High-elevation mine and placer terrain can contain unstable excavations and sudden weather hazards. Stay on lawful public routes, respect closures and private property, and do not enter abandoned workings.
